acceptanceCriteria: index output names the shared store path it wrote and every snapshot it evicted.
Eviction never removes a snapshot whose tree matches a live worktree HEAD, or the policy is documented with a bounded alternative.
A fresh linked worktree whose tree hash already has a snapshot in the common dir reuses it, and its prompt event is not FALLBACK.
Maintained tests cover the eviction report and the reuse.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Source: read-only rc.3 accuracy survey 2026-10-06 (origin/main 3dc863bd, installed rc.2 build 360) replaying merged PRs 571, 614, 594, 557, 610 at their merge-base. Harness and outputs: /private/tmp/claude-501/td-survey (local, not retained in the repository). Running `corvint index --if-stale` in a survey worktree wrote a 124 MB snapshot into the primary checkout's shared .git/corvint/index/ and evicted 2 older snapshots. Concurrent sessions lose their current snapshot and must re-index; the command reports neither the shared write nor the eviction. A fresh worktree's prompt hook also stays FALLBACK (dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale) because index --if-stale takes about 2.0 s, above the 1.6 s dogfoodEventDeadline. Related: V1-0212, V1-0302, V1-0409, V1-0418.

The build-log entry records the change, the maintained tests and the Codex review with its repairs; decision 0438 records the owner's acceptance of IDX-SNAP-V0-025. The batch passed the full doc-gate CI list, the focused package tests and every hosted CI check on the merge head. NOT_RUN: make gate, -race, and live fleet qualification where the spec says so.

title: index --if-stale from a linked worktree writes a ~120 MB snapshot into the shared common dir and evicts other sessions' snapshots without warning
